notes: Iteration 2: with_skill 29/29, without_skill 28/29. Iteration 1 was 28/28 versus 25/28. The gap narrowed because the baseline improved, not because the skill got worse.

The chatId fix works and does not discriminate. The new assertion passes in BOTH configurations: the skill now states it, and the base model already knew it. Fixing that gap brought the skill level with the baseline rather than ahead of it, which is still the right fix.

Iteration 1's eval-3 advantage was largely variance. That baseline scored 4/6; this one scored 7/7 on a superset of the same assertions, naming all four SSE events and the metadata ordering. With one run per configuration, run-to-run variance is indistinguishable from skill effect, so the +3 reported for iteration 1 should be read as noisy.

Exactly ONE assertion now discriminates across both iterations: the archive and version pin on eval-2. That is the only thing the base model provably cannot know, since it postdates training. Every other assertion in the suite measures the model.

The assertions keep missing where the skill actually pays. This iteration the with_skill transfer run produced the finding that Labs prompts are database-backed so the source constants are only a seed, and that extraction backfills searchTerm from name when the prompt omits it. Neither is rewarded by any assertion, and both changed real decisions.
Baselines remain contamination-free: zero mentions of archive, sunset, 3.1.3 or Workday in all five without_skill runs.
Three corrections landed AFTER these runs started (the silent JSON fallback on a non-streamable flow, sessionId bypassing the override gate, the frame format). This iteration does not measure them.

Methodological flaw to fix before iteration 3: the output path names the condition, so a baseline agent can see it is the control arm. One this round said so explicitly and abstained from the skill, which is the honest outcome but not a guaranteed one. Use neutral run directories.
